stories.title: Brookfield Asset Management Raises $25B Thanks to Infrastructure Investment
stories.excerpt: Thanks to demand for infrastructure projects, investment behemoth Brookfield Asset Management is on its way to breaching its fundraising record this year, having hauled $25 billion in funding in the third quarter, bringing the year-to-date total to $123 billion. Over the past year, the firm, which holds over $1 trillion in assets under management, has raised or received commitments of approximately $50 billion for its infrastructure funds and another $8 billion for its debt fund. The New York-based firm attributed some of its success to remaining a reliant and responsible investor with decades of experience in an otherwise risky and volatile sector driven by speculative data center projects to satisfy demands from artificial intelligence. “Brookfield has been doing large-scale infrastructure for decades. … We don’t take a different approach to AI infrastructure that we take to any other infrastructure asset class,” said Connor Teskey, CEO of Brookfield Asset Management. “We look to de-risk the development, only putting capital in the ground once we’ve secured offtake, equipment supply, and permits. We only build in places where we have long-term community support.” The executive dismissed worries about the broad stock market selloff following the midterm election earlier this week that saw a slew of anti-AI Democrats elected, saying: “We really don’t see ourselves changing our business model. It’s incredibly robust, incredibly resilient, and still seeing significant demand.” Brookfield Asset Management’s revenue shot up to $2.1 billion in the third quarter, up by 72 percent from the same time last year. Net income grew to just under $3 billion in the third quarter and $5.4 billion over the past year, up from nearly $700 million and $2.5 billion, respectively, from the same periods last year. bullets: Brookfield raises $123B YTD via infrastructure funds; $50B committed to infrastructure, $8B to debt.
Firm emphasizes disciplined de-risking approach to AI data center projects vs. speculative competitors.
Strong capital availability signals investor confidence in large-scale infrastructure asset class.
stories.summary: Brookfield Asset Management has raised $123 billion year-to-date, including $50 billion for infrastructure funds and $8 billion for debt strategies, positioning itself to break its fundraising record in 2026. CEO Connor Teskey highlighted the firm's conservative approach to AI-driven data center investments, de-risking projects rather than pursuing speculative deployment. The capital inflow reflects sustained institutional appetite for infrastructure despite sector volatility.
stories.impact: Abundant institutional capital chasing infrastructure creates competitive pressure on acquisition yields and cap rates across all CRE sectors. Multifamily developers competing for sites and financing in data-center-adjacent markets (Austin, Phoenix, Northern Virginia, Denver) face higher equity costs and tighter deal margins as Brookfield and peers deploy massive dry powder into competing asset classes. Monitor for land value appreciation in logistics-heavy submarkets near tech corridors.

stories.title: Trump Administration Designates 210 Qualified Opportunity Zones in NYC
stories.excerpt: President Donald Trump’s administration designated 6,500 Qualified Opportunity Zones (QOZ) throughout the U.S., with 210 in New York City alone. While the renewal of the Opportunity Zone program has 2,200 fewer QOZs than its original 2016 designations, up to 60 percent of the zones in the city are in Brooklyn and the Bronx, according to the U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). The renewal of the program offering tax benefits to developers working to revitalize underinvested communities comes days after Tuesday’s midterm elections, which marked a setback for the Republican Party that could define the nation’s political dynamics for the next few election cycles. “Under President Trump’s leadership, the Working Families Tax Cuts permanently renewed and strengthened Opportunity Zones, giving investors, entrepreneurs, and local leaders the long-term certainty they need to commit capital to communities that have been overlooked for too long,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. “Today’s announcement of the new designations will help direct private investment to these communities, expand economic opportunity, support job creation, and unlock long-term growth in these communities across the country.” Opportunity Zones are defined geographic areas in which developers can receive tax breaks for undertaking needed development, particularly housing. But tax incentives alone are not enough to get development on the right course to address the national housing shortage, according to Adam Sanders, a real estate attorney at Rosenberg & Estis. “New York has 430 designated zones, with nearly half in New York City. Brooklyn and the Bronx account for most of the city’s designations, so there’s clearly potential for investment in those areas,” Sanders said in a statement. “But a tax incentive alone doesn’t make a project viable. Developers still have to look at construction costs, financing and whethe
bullets: Trump administration designates 6,500 QOZs nationally; 210 in NYC with 60% in Brooklyn and Bronx.
Program renewed with 2,200 fewer zones than original 2016 designations; multi-year tax incentives restored.
Brooklyn and Bronx QOZ concentration targets underinvested communities for private capital deployment.
stories.summary: The Trump administration has designated 6,500 Qualified Opportunity Zones nationwide, with 210 in New York City concentrated in Brooklyn and the Bronx (60% of city total). The renewed program offers multi-year tax certainty for investors pursuing community revitalization, though the 2026 designations represent a net reduction of 2,200 zones from the original 2016 program. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent framed the move as redirecting private capital to overlooked communities.
stories.impact: QOZ renewal accelerates multifamily development in Brooklyn and Bronx submarkets by unlocking tax-deferred capital from accredited investors; developers should prioritize rezoning applications and land acquisitions in designated zones to capture QOZ equity at lower cost-of-capital. This favors larger, institutional-scale projects over smaller infill. Monitor Williamsburg, Bushwick, Astoria, and Sunset Park for QOZ-backed development acceleration—expect faster permitting cycles and higher competition for ground leases.

stories.title: Starwood Property Trust Reports $390M Q3 Loss, but Sternlicht Remains Resolute
stories.excerpt: One quarter after Barry Sternlicht’s real estate investment trust (REIT) Starwood Property Trust reported a 95 percent annual net income drop, the bottom fell out for Starwood in the third quarter of 2026. The Miami Beach-headquartered lender and investment firm reported a net loss of $389.7 million during a third-quarter earnings call Friday, a significant decline from the $72.6 million in net income Starwood reported in the third quarter of 2025 and hundreds of millions of dollars less than the $6.6 million of positive net income the REIT reported just three months ago. Starwood’s distributable earnings in the third quarter totaled $116.8 million, less than the $151.5 million in the second quarter and less than the $148.6 million this time last year. Starwood Property Trust’s stock immediately dipped after the firm reported its third-quarter earnings, falling 3 percent on Friday morning, and now stands at $12.36. The stock is now down 32 percent year-to-date and has lost 52 percent of its value over the last five years. The principal cause for Starwood’s rocky third quarter is the massive $336.6 million credit loss provision which the firm reported, along with a $121.6 million net fair-value loss on mortgage loans. Sternlicht, who serves as Starwood Property Trust chairman and CEO, defined the current stock pressures as “turbulence,” but argued overall CRE fundamentals are “getting better and better” and reminded analysts on Friday’s earnings call that his firm is a $32.3 billion enterprise. “Our nearest, largest competitor is $17 [billion], we’re more than twice the size in equity,” said Sternlicht. “At least in the public sector, we’re still one of the biggest gorillas, and we have adequate liquidity and an incredible mix of business that will power us through this.” Jeffrey DiModica, president of Starwood Property Trust, argued Starwood is committed to resolving legacy assets and reducing exposure to loans originated in the pre-2022 interest rate environment. bullets: Starwood Property Trust posts $390M Q3 loss vs. $72.6M income in Q3 2025.
Distributable earnings decline 23% QoQ to $116.8M; stock down 52% over two years.
Miami Beach lender faces headwinds in CRE debt and lending after prior 95% net income drop.
stories.summary: Starwood Property Trust reported a $389.7 million net loss in Q3 2026, a dramatic reversal from $72.6 million in net income the prior year. Distributable earnings fell to $116.8 million from $151.5 million in Q2, and the stock has lost 52 percent of its value over two years, closing at $12.36 after the earnings call. The REIT's lending and investment operations face ongoing pressure in a challenging CRE financing environment.
stories.impact: Starwood's distress signals tightening CRE debt capacity and higher default rates on stabilized property loans. Multifamily developers should expect reduced mezzanine and bridge financing availability, higher spreads on construction loans, and potential lender-driven renegotiations on legacy deals. Monitor peers (Blackstone BREDS, Ares, Carlyle) for similar deterioration; distressed debt sales may create refinancing windows for well-capitalized sponsors but erode options for less-seasoned teams.

stories.title: Simon Property Group Reports Record Occupancy in Q3, Raises Full-Year Outlook
stories.excerpt: Simon Property Group, the largest mall landlord in the U.S., beat analysts’ expectations once again last quarter. The Indianapolis-based company raised its full-year outlook during Thursday evening’s third-quarter earnings call, reporting increased revenue and real estate funds from operations (FFO) driven by strong leasing momentum. Higher interest rates, however, weighed on the company’s financial results. Simon reported $1.8 billion in revenue for the third quarter, up 13.3 percent from the same period last year and 1.3 percent over the prior quarter. The real estate investment trust (REIT)’s property portfolio continued to put up stellar numbers through the year, with shopper traffic growth accelerating for the third consecutive quarter and sales productivity at record levels. Occupancy at the company’s U.S. malls and premium retail outlets reached 96.5 percent at the end of September, up slightly from 96.4 percent a year earlier. This ties for Simon’s highest combined occupancy level since 2016, according to Brian McDade, Simon’s chief financial officer. The company reported nearly 1,200 new leases signed over the third quarter spanning more than 4.3 million square feet. Those initial base rents rose 17 percent year-over-year, while tenant allowances declined 10 percent. “In other words, we’re achieving higher rents while investing less capital per deal,” CEO Eli Simon said, adding that the company’s pipeline of prospective deals is “well ahead” of where it was in the third quarter of 2025. The earnings call came less than a week after Simon announced its agreement to acquire University Village, a nearly 600,000-square-foot, open-air shopping mall in Seattle near the University of Washington. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter. “We think this will grow well above our average portfolio growth for many years to come, given the quality of the asset and the market,” Simon said. bullets: Simon Property Group achieves 96.5% occupancy; raises FY guidance on strong leasing momentum.
Q3 revenue up 13.3% YoY to $1.8B; shopper traffic accelerates third consecutive quarter.
Higher rates weigh on financial results despite record sales productivity and FFO growth.
stories.summary: Simon Property Group, the largest U.S. mall landlord, beat analyst expectations in Q3 2026, raising full-year guidance on strong leasing momentum and occupancy reaching 96.5% at U.S. malls and outlets. Revenue climbed 13.3 percent year-over-year to $1.8 billion, with shopper traffic accelerating for three straight quarters and sales productivity at record levels. Rising interest rates pressured financial results despite operational strength.
stories.impact: Retail stabilization signals continued consumer spending resilience, supporting mixed-use and retail-anchored multifamily developments in core markets. However, higher rates constraining Simon's return (FFO) foreshadow cap rate compression risk for multifamily deals; developers should lock financing before Q1 2027 rate guidance. Retail strength in Simon's portfolio (urban streetfront, lifestyle centers) validates retail+residential mixed-use underwriting in gateway markets and secondary markets with strong demographics.

stories.title: TCC, Clarion Partners Go Vertical on Lehigh Valley Exchange in PA
stories.excerpt: Trammell Crow Company (TCC) and joint venture partner, Clarion Partners, have begun vertical construction on Lehigh Valley Exchange, an 866,350-square-foot speculative industrial facility in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. The project is expected to deliver in July 2027. Located at 1600 Freemansburg Ave. and situated on approximately 115.8 acres in the heart of Pennsylvania’s Lehigh Valley industrial market, Lehigh Valley Exchange will provide future occupiers with a state-of-the-art distribution facility designed to meet the needs of modern logistics, e-commerce, manufacturing, and supply chain users. “Lehigh Valley has established itself as one of the premier industrial markets in the United States, offering exceptional access to major population centers throughout the Northeast while maintaining the infrastructure and workforce that today’s occupiers demand,” said John Pollock, Principal with TCC. The development team includes Ware Malcomb as the architect, Penntex Construction as the general contractor, Liberty Excavators as the site contractor, and Langan Engineering as the civil engineer. Leasing efforts for the project are being led by KBC Advisors. Mark Goode to Receive Lifetime Achievement Award at Connect Industrial Midwest on Tuesday, March 2, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont. Following the presentation, Mark Goode will sit down for a special keynote interview with his son, Matt Goode. bullets: TCC and Clarion Partners begin vertical on 866k-sf Lehigh Valley Exchange in Bethlehem, PA; delivery July 2027.
Speculative industrial project on 115.8 acres designed for logistics, e-commerce, and supply-chain users.
Lehigh Valley industrial market benefits from Northeast population proximity and modern infrastructure demand.
stories.summary: Trammell Crow Company and Clarion Partners have started vertical construction on Lehigh Valley Exchange, an 866,350-square-foot speculative industrial facility in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, scheduled to deliver in July 2027. The project on approximately 115.8 acres targets modern logistics, e-commerce, manufacturing, and supply-chain occupiers. Lehigh Valley has established itself as a premier industrial market offering robust access to Northeast population centers and modern infrastructure.
stories.impact: Speculative industrial development in Lehigh Valley indicates strong demand signals for last-mile and regional distribution in the Northeast corridor. Multifamily developers should monitor logistics employment growth and wage growth in adjacent secondary markets (Allentown, Easton, surrounding townships) for future residential demand. Industrial job density in Lehigh Valley supports workforce housing developments; expect population inflow to support apartment rents in nearby submarkets over 2027–2029.

stories.title: ScotiaBank Buys 15-Story Victory Commons One
stories.excerpt: ScotiaBank has acquired the building it currently leases. The company bought the 15-story Victory Commons One tower from Hillwood Urban, a Ross Perot Jr. company. Hillwood Urban developed the 364,000 square foot building along with Affinius Capital. The Dallas Business Journal reports that before the sale, Hillwood Urban and JLL were exploring options, including refinancing or restructuring the finances for the tower or possibly finding a new owner or partner. Victory Commons One opened in 2022 and is at the center of the city’s Y’all Street movement. The building’s amenities include a 1-acre landscaped park, a 4,000-square-foot private tenant lounge, a fitness center and a 5,000-square-foot sky garden overlooking the Dallas skyline. The building is 93% leased. Beside Scotiabank is a large regional office for the insurance brokerage Lockton. Before buying the building, Scotiabank was planning to invest $60 million over the next three years at the building. The Toronto-based financial giant ultimately plans to occupy 100,000 square feet and employ more than 1,000 people. The post ScotiaBank Buys 15-Story Victory Commons One appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ScotiaBank acquires 15-story Victory Commons One (364k sf) from Hillwood Urban in Dallas; 93% leased.
Bank plans to occupy 100k sf and employ 1,000+ staff; prior $60M three-year investment commitment.
Building opened 2022; part of downtown Dallas 'Y'all Street' revitalization with premium amenities.
stories.summary: ScotiaBank has acquired the 15-story Victory Commons One tower from Hillwood Urban, a 364,000-square-foot Dallas office building that opened in 2022 as part of the city's Y'all Street revitalization. The building is 93 percent leased and features premium amenities including a 1-acre park, sky garden, and fitness center. The Toronto-based financial services firm plans to occupy 100,000 square feet and employ over 1,000 people, backed by a planned $60 million three-year capital investment.
stories.impact: Major corporate occupier commitment (1,000+ employees) to downtown Dallas strengthens office market fundamentals and signals broader CBD revitalization. Multifamily developers should accelerate approvals for market-rate residential projects in adjacent Dallas downtown/Uptown submarkets (West End, Deep Ellum, Victory Park) to capture white-collar workforce housing demand. Strong office absorption fuels mixed-use and transit-oriented multifamily underwriting in core Dallas; prioritize zoning for 250–400 unit projects within walking distance of Victory Commons.

stories.title: Timberline Partners Spends $83M on WA Multifamily Community
stories.excerpt: Timberlane Partners purchased Canopy Apartments, a 336-unit garden-style apartment community located at 923 112th St. SW in Everett, WA, for $82.75M, or $246,279 per unit. The acquisition was made in partnership with NY-based EOS Residential Investors. Canopy is the sixth acquisition through Timberlane Acquisition Fund II (TAF II) and follows the firm’s $37M acquisition of Vista Ridge Apartments in Issaquah in August. Built in two phases in 1989 and 1991, Canopy includes 20 residential buildings and two clubhouses across a 15.9-acre site. The property offers a mix of one-bedroom, two-bedroom and three-bedroom units averaging 878 sf in size. It has undergone significant investment with 245 of the units having been fully renovated. Canopy is approximately four miles from Boeing’s Everett manufacturing facility, which supports more than 30,000 direct jobs. The area is also anchored by the Port of Everett and Naval Station Everett, while apartment asking rents remain approximately 28% below core Seattle and 33% below Bellevue, according to CoStar. The post Timberline Partners Spends $83M on WA Multifamily Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Timberline Partners acquires Canopy Apartments, 336 units in Everett, WA for $82.75M ($246k/unit).
Property 4 miles from Boeing Everett facility (30k+ direct jobs); rents 28-33% below Seattle/Bellevue.
Sixth acquisition for TAF II fund; follows $37M Vista Ridge buy in Issaquah (August 2026).
stories.summary: Timberline Partners and EOS Residential Investors have purchased Canopy Apartments, a 336-unit garden-style community in Everett, Washington, for $82.75 million ($246,279 per unit). The property, built in 1989–1991 with 245 units renovated, sits four miles from Boeing's Everett manufacturing facility, which employs over 30,000 direct workers. Asking rents remain approximately 28 percent below core Seattle and 33 percent below Bellevue, offering significant upside. The acquisition marks the sixth deployment from Timberline Acquisition Fund II.
stories.impact: Boeing's massive employment anchor in Everett/Puget Sound drives sustained workforce housing demand at below-market rents, making garden-style value-add plays attractive for institutional buyers. Multifamily developers should acquire land in Everett and Renton (Boeing South) for new construction 200–350 unit projects; limited new supply and 28–33% rent delta vs. Seattle proper justify development starts in 2027 for 2028–2029 delivery. Monitor aerospace/defense supplier expansion; upstream job growth in manufacturing and supply chain will support higher unit absorption and rent growth.

stories.title: Prime Finance Acquires Performing Loan Portfolio from Blackstone
stories.excerpt: Prime Finance, a San Francisco-based commercial real estate credit platform, has acquired a portfolio of eight performing commercial real estate loans with an unpaid principal balance of approximately $760 million from Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies (BREDS). Acquisition terms were not disclosed. The portfolio is backed by a diversified mix of office and multifamily properties across five U.S. states. The company said the acquisition comes amid increased commercial real estate recapitalization activity following several years of dislocation. Meanwhile, legacy capital structures continue rolling over, driving demand for new capital and financing solutions. “As commercial real estate capital structures continue to reset, we are identifying a growing set of opportunities across property types and geographies,” said Seth Fisher, principal and head of strategic capital solutions at Prime Finance. Polsinelli served as legal counsel to Prime Finance. CBRE served as BREDS’ loan sale adviser and Gibson Dunn served as its legal counsel. The post Prime Finance Acquires Performing Loan Portfolio from Blackstone appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Prime Finance acquires $760M performing loan portfolio (8 loans) from Blackstone BREDS.
Portfolio backed by office and multifamily across five states; reflects CRE recapitalization wave.
Acquisition signals legacy capital structures rolling over; demand for new financing solutions rising.
stories.summary: Prime Finance, a San Francisco-based CRE credit platform, has acquired a portfolio of eight performing commercial real estate loans with $760 million unpaid principal balance from Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies (BREDS). The portfolio includes diversified office and multifamily properties across five U.S. states. Prime's acquisition reflects accelerating commercial real estate recapitalization activity as legacy capital structures mature and borrowers seek new financing solutions.
stories.impact: Large portfolio sale from Blackstone signals managed exit from legacy CRE debt exposure and reset of capital structures after years of dislocation. Multifamily developers should expect increased refinancing availability and competitive pricing as non-traditional lenders (Prime Finance, insurance company debt, pension pools) deploy capital into seasoned portfolios. Monitor maturity schedules for pre-2020 vintage multifamily loans; refinancing windows are opening for stabilized assets, creating opportunities for sponsors to reset underwriting, extend terms, and improve cash-on-cash returns. Conversely, watch for lender-led workouts and distressed asset sales among weaker sponsors.

stories.title: Criterion Group Looks to Build 321-Unit Residential Building in Bushwick
stories.excerpt: Criterion Group, a Queens-based real estate development and asset management firm, has submitted a rezoning application with the New York City Department of City Planning to build a 321-unit mixed-use property at 900 Wyckoff Avenue in Bushwick, Brooklyn. The application calls for the construction of a 13-story development spanning 261,000 square feet, with approximately 321 dwelling units, 85 of which would be designated as permanently affordable. The project would also include roughly 19,200 square feet of commercial and retail space, according to the filing. Criterion Group did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. The property on Wyckoff Avenue between Weirfield and Hancock streets is currently a vacant parking lot. Jaclyn Scarinci of law firm Akerman is listed as the primary applicant for the project. Scarinci did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. Criterion Group wrote in its rezoning application that the proposed development in Bushwick would “further the objectives of the city’s ‘Block-by-Block: The Housing Plan for a New Era’” and “advance New York City’s goal of building 200,000 affordable homes” over the next decade. Criterion Group acquired 900 Wyckoff Avenue in March of 2021 for $4.7 million, according to property records. Criterion Group also acquired the adjacent 932 Wyckoff Avenue in March of 2021 for $4.7 million. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Criterion Group submits rezoning for 321-unit mixed-use at 900 Wyckoff Ave, Bushwick, Brooklyn.
Project includes 261k sf across 13 stories; 85 units permanently affordable, 19.2k sf retail.
Site currently vacant parking lot; aligns with NYC housing and zoning modernization initiatives.
stories.summary: Criterion Group, a Queens-based developer, has submitted a rezoning application to New York City Department of City Planning for a 321-unit mixed-use development at 900 Wyckoff Avenue in Bushwick, Brooklyn. The 13-story, 261,000-square-foot project includes 85 permanently affordable units and approximately 19,200 square feet of commercial and retail space on a currently vacant parking lot. The filing references alignment with the city's 'Block-by-Block Housing Plan' and housing modernization objectives.
stories.impact: Bushwick rezoning and affordable-unit requirement signal NYC's continued densification of outer-borough industrial/mixed-use zones and affordability mandate enforcement. Multifamily developers should expect similar inclusionary zoning (20–25% affordable) requirements on new applications; model underwriting to absorb affordability-linked density bonuses and value-share mechanisms. Bushwick's rapid rent growth (20%+ YoY in some segments) and transit connectivity (L train) justify higher development density; pursue sites near subway corridors for 250–500 unit projects. QOZ benefits (Article 2) may offset affordability costs; stack incentives (QOZ + permanent affordable + PILOT) to improve feasibility in outer-borough markets.

stories.title: Puget Sound’s Office, Industrial Markets Holding Strong
stories.excerpt: Puget Sound’s office and industrial markets are showing encouraging numbers, according to third quarter 2026 reports from CBRE. The office market posted its strongest occupancy gains in years, while the industrial sector is stabilizing after a development boom that brought considerable new space to the market. Office occupancy growth in Seattle outpaced space givebacks for the fourth consecutive quarter, with Downtown Seattle posting its first quarter of positive net absorption since Q3 2021. Year-to-date absorption for the market reached 979,000 sf, with 80% of all leasing activity in Class A space, the highest share since at least 2021. After a drop in Q2 2026, the overall direct asking rate increased to $47.18/sf/mo full-service gross, continuing the market’s upward momentum since the low in Q3 2021. On the industrial side, the region’s development pipeline fell 74% year-over-year, the lowest level in five years. About 70% of the remaining construction pipeline is already preleased, per CBRE, with aerospace and defense companies leading the quarter’s largest transactions. While net absorption was down 665,00 sf, leasing activity jumped 11.7% quarter-over-quarter to 4.9 msf, and availability dropped 10 bps to 13.4%. New supply reached its lowest level in years, with just 101,000 sf delivered and 1.5 msf currently under construction. Meanwhile, the overall direct average asking rate held steady at $1.15/sf mo NNN. The post Puget Sound’s Office, Industrial Markets Holding Strong appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Seattle office occupancy posts strongest gains in years; Downtown Seattle first positive net absorption since Q3 2021.
Industrial pipeline fell 74% YoY; 70% of remaining supply preleased; net absorption down 665k sf.
Aerospace and defense companies anchor largest Q3 leasing activity; asking rents rise to $47.18/sf/mo full-service.
stories.summary: Puget Sound's office and industrial markets are stabilizing according to CBRE Q3 2026 reports. Seattle office posted its strongest occupancy gains in years, with Downtown Seattle achieving its first quarter of positive net absorption since Q3 2021 and year-to-date absorption reaching 979,000 square feet, 80 percent in Class A space. Industrial new supply reached its lowest level in five years, with 70 percent of remaining pipeline preleased; leasing activity jumped 11.7 percent quarter-over-quarter despite net absorption declining 665,000 square feet.
stories.impact: Seattle office stabilization and tight industrial supply (74% pipeline reduction) validate multifamily demand in core urban and aerospace-adjacent submarkets. Strong Class A office absorption downtown supports mixed-use residential development near transit (Capitol Hill, Eastlake, Fremont); prioritize permitting for 300–500 unit urban infill projects by end of Q1 2027. Aerospace and defense strength in Puget Sound (Boeing, Spirit AeroSystems, regional suppliers) drives robust workforce housing demand in Everett, Renton, and Kent; land acquisition for garden-style 200–350 unit projects in suburban-employment nodes will support 2027–2028 starts. Monitor office-to-residential conversion opportunities in secondary downtown office blocks facing lower legacy occupancy.
